title: Automated Optimize Suggestion Rollout Policy Manager
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a rollout policy manager that safely auto-applies Optimize's batching and caching recommendations. It should provide gated rollouts, fine-grained canary segmentation, approval hooks, audit trails, and automated rollback triggers so teams can capture cost savings while preserving latency and quality SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Console UI: a policy page where a PM or engineer can create a rollout policy referencing an Optimize suggestion and select gating controls (percent ramp, target routes/customers, time window).
Canary engine: traffic can be split by percent, model variant, customer tier, route, or region with optional request shadowing for dry-run verification.
Automated checks: pre-apply simulation and post-apply monitors including p95 latency delta, error rate, token cost per request, and quality regression alerts tied to evaluation prompts.
Approval flows: policy supports manual approval, auto-approve after dry-run passes, or scheduled approvals integrated with GitHub PR and Slack notifications.
Rollback: automatic rollback on configurable triggers (latency > 20% p95, error rate spike, cost increase threshold, or quality regression), with immediate notification and audit log entry.
Auditability: every policy change and automated action emits an immutable audit event with operator, timestamp, and linked artifacts (PR/Confluence).
technical_design: Policy model: store policies as atomic records referencing suggestion_id, target selector (routes/models/customers/regions), ramp schedule, rollback thresholds, approval mode, and metadata tags.
Controller: Kubernetes-style reconciliation loop that transitions suggestions through states (Draft -> DryRun -> Canary -> Ramp -> Stable -> Rollback) and emits events.

Dry-run path: duplicate requests via non-blocking shadowing to candidate config with metrics collection but no user-visible impact. Use sample-based KV cache warmup to approximate steady-state savings.
Canary enforcement: traffic-splitting via edge/routing layer (Envoy + internal router flags). Percent-based ramp executed in steps (default 5% every 10 minutes) with cooldown windows.

Safety checks: lightweight, fast checks (p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate) computed from streaming telemetry; heavier quality checks run on sampled responses against golden prompt sets and run asynchronously.
Approval integration: webhook-based hooks to GitHub (create PR with policy diff), and Slack/Console notifications. Allow external approval by marking policy approved in Console or merging PR.
State machine persistence: use existing config-store (etcd-backed) with versioning; each config apply creates a signed release blob for audit and rollback.
Circuit breaker: if controller detects metrics staleness or backend failures, it pauses ramp and optionally reverses last step instead of continuing.
Telemetry: emit structured events for policy lifecycle (policy.created, policy.dryrun.started, policy.canary.step, policy.rolledback) to observability pipeline for dashboards and alerts.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Week 1): Infrastructure plumbing - config-store, controller scaffolding, and event schema. Test local reconciliation loop.
Phase 2 (Week 2): Implement dry-run shadowing path and sampling harness. Run internal simulation traffic and compare cost estimates.
Phase 3 (Week 3): Canary split implementation + Console UI for policy creation. Integrate Slack/GitHub approval flows.
Phase 4 (Week 4): Safety checks, thresholds UI, and rollback automation. End-to-end test with staged customers/internal accounts.
Phase 5 (Week 5): Gradual rollout to customers using feature flag; collect metrics, run quality evals, and tune defaults.
Phase 6 (Post rollout): Documentation, runbook, and handoff to SRE/Customer Success for operationalization.
monitoring_and_alerting: Primary metrics: p95 latency delta (canary vs baseline), 5xx rate delta, token_cost_per_request delta, sampled quality_score delta.
Alerts: critical alert if p95 increases > 20% sustained for 3 minutes or 5xx rate spike > 5x baseline; warning if cost per request increases > 15%.
Dashboards: per-policy dashboard showing ramp %, metric deltas, approval state, last action, and recent audit events.
Quality pipeline: nightly batch of golden prompts evaluated on canary subset with regression score and PR triage link when regressions exceed threshold.
Notifications: Slack channel + Ops PagerDuty escalation on critical rollback. Email summaries to policy owners on completion.
rollback_strategy: Multi-tier rollback: 1) automatic step-back: if a single ramp step triggers thresholds, controller reduces to previous safe step. 2) full immediate rollback: if catastrophic (p95 > 50% or 5xx > 10x), revert to last stable config and mark policy as RolledBack. 3) manual rollback: policy owner can trigger revert from Console or merge a rollback PR. All rollbacks create an audit record and annotate the Optimize suggestion with failure reason.
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for reconciliation state transitions and policy validation rules.
Integration tests that spin up controller against a local router mock and verify traffic-splitting behavior.
E2E harness: replay production traces against two configs to validate cost delta, latency impact, and cache effectiveness estimates.
Chaos tests: simulate metric staleness and partial failures to verify circuit-breaker behavior.
Security review: ensure policy creation and approval endpoints require RBAC permission checks; include penetration test in staging.
